title: Time Jump: 14:00 Wednesday, Six Hours to the Order Deadline

fields.scenarioTitle: Eighteen Hours: Rising Crest, Evacuation Clock & Levee Fight
fields.narration: EXERCISE EXERCISE EXERCISE. It is now 14:00 CDT, Wednesday 21 April 2027. Two hours have passed since the National Weather Service issued its 12:00 flood warning. The Cedar River at Cedar Ford, CFDI4 on the Route 38 bridge piers, reads 16.0 feet and is rising about 0.13 feet an hour. It went above flood stage this morning and has stayed there. The forecast in force is the 12:00 Wednesday issuance. It calls for major flooding, with a crest near 23.4 feet at 06:00 Saturday, up from 21.8 feet at 20:00 Friday. The river is now expected to reach 19.0 feet, the level at which Cedar Hollow floods, around 14:00 Thursday. That is about 18 hours earlier than the previous forecast said. Public Works has had River Road south of Mill Street barricaded since about 07:30. The Riverside Park lot is under water, and Water Street basements are taking water. The Cedar Hollow advisory has not been updated since the noon product. Under the 12:00 issuance, the deadline for the Cedar Hollow evacuation order is 20:00 tonight, six hours from now. The receiving care home, the co-op's cattle truckers, Tallis Valley Radio and the school district have all called back, and each wants an answer this afternoon. The day crews have been working since 07:00. The clock is running.
worldState: Time: 14:00 CDT, Wednesday 21 April 2027.
CFDI4 (Route 38 bridge piers): 16.0 ft and rising about 0.13 ft an hour. That is above flood stage (15.0 ft) and 1.0 ft below the Mill Street underpass closure stage (17.0 ft).

Forecast in force: NWS Quad Cities, 12:00 PM CDT Wednesday issuance. MAJOR flooding, crest near 23.4 ft at 06:00 Saturday. The river is forecast to pass 17.0 ft late tonight and 19.0 ft around 14:00 Thursday. No newer issuance has been received.

The 23.4 ft crest is at or above major (23.0 ft). At that stage the forecast expects levee seepage, and the 340 homes behind the levee are at risk. At 22.5 ft, interior ponding reaches the wastewater plant yard if Pump Stations 1 and 2 fall behind.
Cedar Hollow: the voluntary advisory has had no update since the noon product. The deadline for the mandatory order is 20:00 Wednesday (18 hours before 19.0 ft). No order has been issued.
Hollow Court Care Center (36 residents) needs 12 hours to clear. Its vans and its receiving facility are still not confirmed.
River Road south of Mill Street has been barricaded since about 07:30. The Mill Street underpass is open, and the city's four barricades are staged nearby. Route 38 bottoms are open.
The Riverside Park lot is under water, and Water Street basements are wet.
Tallis Prairie Cooperative's feed yard floods at 19 ft. It takes 24 hours and 14 cattle trucks to move the herd, and the truckers are waiting for a firm answer.
Callbacks waiting: the receiving care home, the co-op general manager, the Tallis Valley Radio reporter and the school district.
Day shift crews (Public Works, Levee District patrols, deputies, Fire) have been on duty since 07:00.
fields.facilitatorNote: Players should count back from 19.0 ft at 14:00 Thursday, not from the 06:00 Saturday crest. That gives an order deadline of 20:00 tonight under EOP 6.1. Watch for anyone still working from the 18.2 ft or 21.8 ft forecasts. Prompt the group if no one notices two things: the 24-hour lead time for the cattle move (14:00 Wednesday) has already arrived, and a crest of 23.4 ft now meets the 23.0 ft threshold for a disaster declaration request (EOP 6.6).

instructorNote: This card resets the room on the 12:00 issuance and the 16.0 ft reading. The Coordinator should count back from 19.0 ft at 14:00 Thursday, confirm 20:00 Wednesday as the order deadline under EOP 6.1, and recognize that the major-crest triggers (≥23.0 ft) are now live. Watch for anyone still planning from the crest time or a superseded forecast.
